title: fix(gmail): recover watcher after transient restart bind conflicts
body:
Related: #161467

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Gmail forwarding staying down after a Gateway restart briefly overlaps another listener on the watcher's port. Thanks to @kazuyuki-eguchi for the report and restart trace.

## User Impact

The Gateway-managed Gmail watcher recovers automatically when the conflicting listener releases its port within the bounded retry window. A persistent conflict still stops retries and now reports an error with recovery guidance. No configuration or stored-data changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Instead of permanently stopping on the first bind error, the existing respawn lifecycle retries after 5, 10, and 20 seconds using the shared backoff helper. Shutdown cancels pending retries, ordinary exits keep their existing restart policy, and watch renewal continues if the bind retries are exhausted. This preserves the protection against endless duplicate-start loops described in #65042.

## Evidence

- Built baseline and candidate through `pnpm openclaw` and ran real isolated Gateways with a local fake `gog` executable (real TCP bind; no Google account or model requests).
- Started the watcher successfully, stopped the Gateway, held the watcher port with a local listener across replacement Gateway startup, observed `EADDRINUSE`, then released the port after two seconds. Baseline remained down (`Connection refused`); candidate retried after five seconds and returned `fixture watcher alive` over HTTP.
- Persistent-port control: candidate retried after 5/10/20 seconds, emitted `gog serve failed to bind after 3 retries`, and made no further attempts during an additional 25-second observation. All proof Gateways stopped cleanly.
- Regression failed on baseline (expected replacement child, none spawned) and passed on candidate. Focused watcher and foreground Gmail service suites: **31 tests passed**, 30.20 seconds wall including preparation. New/changed bind cases took 2–4 ms. Covers retry cancellation, split/truncated stderr markers, bounded retries, and continued renewal.
- Real Gmail registration/delivery is not exercised: the local fake replaces the external `gog` service, not Gateway lifecycle code.

### Review follow-up

The foreground CLI reference now describes the same bounded retries and continued renewal as the shared watcher service.

Recovery is intentionally bounded to three retries over approximately 35 seconds; a listener that outlasts that window requires operator intervention, as the persistent-port control demonstrates. This patch does not claim that every stale listener exits within that window or fix the earlier shutdown exception in the report.

### Published updater follow-up

Installed unmodified `openclaw@2026.9.6` (`eb377ac`) in a task-owned npm prefix and started its real Gateway/Gmail watcher against the local fake. The watcher responded over HTTP, and Gateway shutdown exited 0 with the listener port free in **4.113 seconds**, within the retry window.

Built and integrity-checked the package from exact PR head `25cb3148657a73c3b81d954830d9591bcbdba982`. Against the existing isolated state, the published updater's `update --tag <candidate.tgz> --no-restart --yes --json` passed candidate configuration, plugin, recovery, and Gateway startup validation, but **failed activation** with:

```text
managed-service-stop-failed:
existing managed handoff lease is incompatible; retain diagnostics and run openclaw triage manually
```

A control used a fresh published prefix and equivalent isolated state, targeting packed `origin/main` **51bc96cacac** instead. That update succeeded in 128.058 seconds with `status: ok` and `serviceRestartSafe: true`; its published watcher released the port in 4.018 seconds.

Both packages used the same self-contained command and flags: `node scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs --allow-unreleased-changelog --output-dir <dir> --output-name <name>`, including full builds and successful tarball integrity checks. No packaging difference was found.

To distinguish the first failure from a deterministic candidate defect, repeated the candidate cell **once** with the **same unchanged tarball** in a fresh prefix and isolated state. Published `2026.9.6` created the state and served the fake Gmail watcher; its listener disappeared in **3.870 seconds** on shutdown. Its unmodified updater then **succeeded in 101.780 seconds**, installing `2026.9.6 (25cb314)`.

The installed candidate, on that existing state, recovered from a real transient port conflict and returned `fixture watcher alive` over HTTP. A persistent-port control made exactly four attempts (initial plus three retries), emitted the terminal error, and made no more attempts during a further 25 seconds. Both installed-candidate Gateways exited 0.

The first lease failure remains an unexplained non-reproducing updater failure, not a claimed fix. It occurred at activation after all candidate checks had succeeded. The published watcher was already stopped; candidate rehearsal disables hooks (`src/infra/update-candidate-rehearsal.ts:120`), so the changed watcher retry loop does not run in that validation path. No updater, lease, shutdown, schema, or additional watcher changes were made to obtain the successful repeat.

A second fresh-prefix candidate repeat also succeeded (**96.601 seconds**, exit 0; published watcher released its listener in **3.897 seconds**). Thus the first activation failure did not recur in **two fresh runs of the identical candidate tarball**. The code-path boundary also excludes this diff from activation: the published watcher has exited before updating, the rehearsal disables hooks, and this PR changes no activation/lease code.
